title: Toilet Refill-Cycle Leak Fingerprint
dataSources: Whole-home water flow (`watermeter:flow`), water pressure (`waterpressure:reading`), irrigation control (`irrigation:zone`), water-heater events (`waterheater:event`), greywater tanks (`greywater:tank`), and utility sensors for pumps and softeners (`sumppump:event`, `wellpump:event`, `watersoftener:status`).
app: Water and plumbing telemetry from smart water meters, pressure sensors, irrigation controllers, sump and well pumps, greywater tanks, and water-heater sensors streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT and vendor APIs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=watermeter:flow fixture="toilet"
| bin _time span=30m
| stats count as refill_events avg(flow_liters) as avg_cycle_liters by bathroom _time
| where refill_events>3
description: Looks for unusually frequent refill cycles from the same toilet, a classic sign of a flapper or valve leak.
value: Toilet leaks are easy to miss but costly over time, and repeated refill fingerprints are often the earliest practical signal.
implementation: Tag fixture-level water events from an instrumented toilet or a smart meter classifier and review short repeat cycles.
visualization: Timeline of refill-event counts by bathroom.
grandmaExplanation: It tracks when the same toilet keeps topping itself up over and over, which usually means water is leaking away.
